enriched.summary: A aula aborda vocabulário comum, incluindo palavras e expressões úteis, além de revisar estruturas gramaticais básicas como formação de frases afirmativas, negativas e interrogativas no presente simples. Também inclui prática de pronúncia e uso de verbos irregulares em diferentes contextos.

vocabulary.definition: Refers to the greater part of a group of people working together.
examples: Most of the team agrees with the proposal.

vocabulary.definition: Happening one time during a week.
examples: She visits her grandmother once a week.

vocabulary.definition: A short phrase or expression that conveys a common truth or piece of wisdom.
examples: There's an old saying: 'Actions speak louder than words.'
I get very anxious before exams.

vocabulary.definition: The process of preserving or keeping something in good condition.
People with whom one works in a professional setting.
The son of one's brother or sister.
examples: My nephew loves playing video games.

vocabulary.definition: The daughter of one's brother or sister.
examples: I bought a gift for my niece's birthday.

vocabulary.definition: To spend time doing something unproductive.
examples: Don't waste time on things that don't matter.

vocabulary.definition: A device or situation designed to catch someone or something.
examples: Be careful not to fall into the trap of procrastination.

grammar.explanation: The present simple is used to describe habits, routines, general truths, and fixed arrangements.
rules: Add '-s' or '-es' to the verb for third-person singular subjects.
Use the base form of the verb for all other subjects.
For negatives, use 'do not' or 'does not' + base form of the verb.
For questions, invert 'do/does' and the subject.
examples: Jane doesn’t speak German at work.
Does Jane speak German at work?
commonMistakes: Forgetting to add '-s' for third-person singular subjects.
Using 'do not' instead of 'does not' with third-person singular subjects.

expressions.usage: Used to discuss inefficient use of time.
examples: Don't waste time on things that aren't important.

practiceQuestions.question: Transform the sentence into a question: 'Jane buys roses every Saturday.'
practiceQuestions.answer: Does Jane buy roses every Saturday?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In the present simple, use 'does' for questions with third-person singular subjects and the base form of the verb.

practiceQuestions.question: Correct the sentence: 'He don't speak Spanish.'
practiceQuestions.explanation: In negative sentences in the present simple, use 'doesn't' for third-person singular subjects.

culturalNotes: In English-speaking countries, titles like 'nephew' and 'niece' are often used to refer to family members in a formal way.
Expressions like 'waste time' are common in workplace and academic contexts to emphasize productivity.
studyTips: Practice forming sentences in the present simple using different subjects and verbs.
Memorize irregular verbs and their forms to avoid mistakes in conjugation.
Use flashcards to remember vocabulary and their translations.
originalExamples: Most of the team. (A maioria do time.)
Once a week. (Uma vez por semana.)
I get very nervous / anxious. (Eu fico muito nervoso / ansioso.)
Waste time: desperdiçar tempo. (Waste time: desperdiçar tempo.)
Jane speaks German at work. (Jane fala alemão no trabalho.)
Jane doesn’t speak German at work. (Jane não fala alemão no trabalho.)
Does Jane speak German at work? (Jane fala alemão no trabalho?)
No, she doesn’t. (Não, ela não fala.)
What language does Jane speak at work? (Que idioma Jane fala no trabalho?)
Mary buys roses every Saturday. (Mary compra rosas todo sábado.)
